facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
noted by his wife to have recently grown and acquired a crust
a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid without margin involvement
the tumor had acquired a flakier surface
The specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
Negative results with Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains
Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei

concepts.why: The presence of a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts, proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, and malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli support this diagnosis.

The yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule and the presence of clear cell change that is periodic acid-Schiff positive and diastase sensitive could suggest sebaceous carcinoma, although the negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin reduce the likelihood.

The well-circumscribed papule and the presence of a hyperkeratotic lesion could also suggest basal cell carcinoma, but the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells and the presence of malignant squamous cells make this less likely.

The presence of a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and the clear cell change that is periodic acid-Schiff positive and diastase sensitive could also suggest keratoacanthoma, but the malignant features and the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells make this less likely.

rationales.F06: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts is characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma and keratoacanthoma.
rationales.F07: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells is typical of squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F08: Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli are characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Negative Alcian blue and mucicarmine stains help rule out sebaceous carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor help rule out sebaceous carcinoma.
rationales.F12: Ki67 staining highlights the proliferative activity of the tumor cells, which is higher in squamous cell carcinoma than in basal cell carcinoma or keratoacanthoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures and the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells into the dermis, strongly supports this diagnosis.
